title: Chicken Chasseur
subtitle: French hunter's chicken in tomato and mushroom sauce
excerpt: Chicken chasseur (hunter's chicken): browned chicken pieces braised in a vibrant sauce of white wine, tomatoes, shallots, tarragon, and mushrooms. One of the great French bistro dishes and ideal for making ahead.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken chasseur (poulet chasseur, or chicken 'hunter style') is a classic French braise based on the ingredients associated with game hunting: mushrooms gathered from the woods, tomatoes, wine, and aromatic herbs. The dish is found across French regional cooking and in Italian cuisine (as pollo alla cacciatora). The French version typically uses white wine and tarragon; the Italian version uses red wine and rosemary or oregano. The sauce is built on a reduction of shallots, white wine, and tomatoes with mushrooms added late to keep their texture. Tarragon is the characteristic French herb here; its anise-like note is essential to the dish's character. The dish is excellent made ahead as the sauce deepens overnight.

content.text: Brown the chicken thoroughly on all sides before braising; the colour provides both flavour and appearance. Tarragon is essential to the French version; do not substitute with other herbs. The sauce should be thick enough to coat the chicken by the end of cooking; if it looks thin, remove the chicken and reduce it briefly.

Season the chicken and brown in the oil in a large casserole over high heat until deeply golden on all sides. Remove. Cook the shallots in the same pot for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato puree, and mushrooms. Cook for 3 minutes.

Add the white wine and reduce by half. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, tarragon, and bay. Return the chicken, skin-side up. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the lid. If the sauce is thin, remove the chicken and reduce the sauce over high heat for 5 minutes. Taste and season. Scatter with parsley. Serve with mashed potato, rice, or crusty bread.
